Every converted chapter in [*ggplot2: field manual*](https://mjfrigaard.github.io/fm-ggp2/) uses simulated data with a late 90s theme, and each dataset gets a `ggplot2` theme to match. This vignette shows each theme with the data from the chapter that introduced it.

Themes with a dark background also have a light version. Set `mode = "light"` to get a light background with darker text and marks. Dark is the default. Each dark theme's section below shows both versions.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
library(fmggp2)
library(ggplot2)
showtext::showtext_auto()
```

## 3Com Audrey

`theme_audrey()` uses a 3Com Audrey on a kitchen counter: a white plastic background, a black tile frame, a teal title, teal, navy, tan, brown, and aqua marks, and an Arial Rounded title. Below we simulate what 300 households used their Audrey for.

![Image: Andrew Turner, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:3Com_Audrey.jpg), CC BY 2.0.](../man/figures/theme_audrey/3com-audrey.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: audrey
set.seed(2000)
uses <- data.frame(month = rep(c("Oct", "Nov", "Dec"), each = 300),
  task = sample(c("Email", "Weather", "Recipes", "Calendar", "Browsing"), 900, replace = TRUE))
uses$month <- factor(uses$month, levels = c("Oct", "Nov", "Dec"))
ggplot(uses, aes(x = month, fill = task)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(title = "Audrey at home", caption = "Simulated data", x = NULL, y = "Share of households", fill = NULL) +
  theme_audrey(base_size = 13)
```

## AIM

`theme_aim()`: the sign on window's gray, AOL blue, sky blue, and the yellow running man. Below we simulate buddy list sizes with different shapes.

![Image: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:AIM_logo.svg), public domain.](../man/figures/theme_aim/aim-logo.png){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: aim
set.seed(1997)
buddies <- data.frame(school = rep(c("Middle school", "College"), each = 150))
buddies$n <- ifelse(buddies$school == "Middle school", rpois(300, 20), ifelse(runif(300) < 0.7, rnorm(300, 60, 10), rnorm(300, 150, 20)))
ggplot(buddies, aes(x = school, y = n, fill = school)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 2/3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "AIM buddy lists (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Buddies") +
  theme_aim(base_size = 13)
```

## Batman

`theme_batman()` comes in three versions. The default, `version = "movie"`, uses the Batman (1989) palette: black, gold, orange, and steel. Below we simulate bat signal sightings over a week.

![Image: Mbrickn, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pop_Culture_Library_Batman_Conference.jpg), CC BY-SA 4.0.](../man/figures/theme_batman/pop-culture-library-batman-conference.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: batman
set.seed(1989)
signals <- data.frame(night = factor(c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"), levels = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")), sightings = rpois(7, 12))
ggplot(signals, aes(x = night, y = sightings)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(title = "Bat signal sightings (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Sightings") +
  theme_batman(base_size = 13)
```

With `mode = "light"`:

```{r}
#| label: batman-light
last_plot() + theme_batman(base_size = 13, mode = "light")
```

`version = "classic"` uses the 1966 TV series palette: gray, blue, yellow, black, and cream.

![](../man/figures/theme_batman/classic-pal.png){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: batman-classic
ggplot(signals, aes(x = night, y = sightings)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(title = "Bat signal sightings (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Sightings") +
  theme_batman(base_size = 13, version = "classic")
```

`version = "darknight"` uses The Dark Knight palette: yellow, olive, charcoal, navy, and slate.

![](../man/figures/theme_batman/darknight-pal.png){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: batman-darknight
ggplot(signals, aes(x = night, y = sightings)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(title = "Bat signal sightings (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Sightings") +
  theme_batman(base_size = 13, version = "darknight")
```

With `mode = "light"`:

```{r}
#| label: batman-darknight-light
last_plot() + theme_batman(base_size = 13, version = "darknight", mode = "light")
```

## Blockbuster

`theme_blockbuster()` uses Blockbuster Video blue and yellow. Below we simulate weekly rentals for 60 households from a Poisson distribution.

![Image: Jon Konrath from Oakland, USA, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Anchorage_Blockbuster_video_store_sign_(41219885734).jpg), CC BY 2.0.](../man/figures/theme_blockbuster/anchorage-blockbuster-video-store-sign-41219885734.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: blockbuster
set.seed(1993)
blockbuster_rentals <- data.frame(rentals = rpois(n = 60, lambda = 3))
ggplot(blockbuster_rentals, aes(x = rentals)) +
  geom_dotplot(binwidth = 1, dotsize = 0.3) +
  labs(title = "Blockbuster Video (simulated)",
       x = "Number of rentals") +
  theme_blockbuster(base_size = 13)
```

With `mode = "light"`:

```{r}
#| label: blockbuster-light
last_plot() + theme_blockbuster(base_size = 13, mode = "light")
```

## Bop It

`theme_bopit()`: Bop It yellow on deep purple, with a purple to yellow continuous scale. Below we simulate reaction times to two commands.

![Image: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bop_It_logo.svg), public domain.](../man/figures/theme_bopit/bop-it-logo.png){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: bopit
set.seed(1996)
players <- data.frame(bop = rnorm(300, 450, 60))
players$twist <- 60 + 0.9 * players$bop + rnorm(300, 0, 40)
ggplot(players, aes(x = bop, y = twist)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = twist), show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Bop It reaction times", caption = "Simulated data", x = "Bop it! (ms)", y = "Twist it! (ms)") +
  theme_bopit(base_size = 13)
```

With `mode = "light"`:

```{r}
#| label: bopit-light
last_plot() + theme_bopit(base_size = 13, mode = "light")
```

## Console wars

`theme_consolewars()`: Sega blue vs. Nintendo red on charcoal. Below we simulate games owned and hours played for two consoles.

![Image: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Sega-Genesis-NA-Mk2-Console-Set.png), public domain.](../man/figures/theme_consolewars/sega-genesis-na-mk2-console-set.png){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

![Image: Digital Game Museum, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Super_Nintendo_(7973380020).jpg), CC BY 2.0.](../man/figures/theme_consolewars/super-nintendo-7973380020.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: consolewars
set.seed(1991)
kids <- data.frame(console = rep(c("Genesis", "SNES"), each = 60), games = rnorm(120, 11, 3))
kids$hours <- 2 + 0.6 * kids$games + ifelse(kids$console == "SNES", 2, 0) + rnorm(120, 0, 2)
ggplot(kids, aes(x = games, y = hours, color = console)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "The console wars", caption = "Simulated data", x = "Games owned", y = "Hours per week", color = NULL) +
  theme_consolewars(base_size = 13)
```

With `mode = "light"`:

```{r}
#| label: consolewars-light
last_plot() + theme_consolewars(base_size = 13, mode = "light")
```

## CU-SeeMe

`theme_cuseeme()` uses the CU-SeeMe phone book window: a dithered gray background, a black frame, a white panel, black, magenta, and gray marks, and a magenta Tahoma title. Below we simulate video call frame rates over three kinds of connections.

![Image: Lt Georgios Floros, HN, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:CU-SeeMe_application_screenshot.png), public domain.](../man/figures/theme_cuseeme/cu-seeme-application-screenshot.png){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: cuseeme
set.seed(1995)
calls <- data.frame(connection = rep(c("28.8k modem", "ISDN", "T1"), each = 60))
calls$fps <- pmax(0.5, rnorm(180, c("28.8k modem" = 2, "ISDN" = 6, "T1" = 14)[calls$connection], 1.5))
ggplot(calls, aes(x = connection, y = fps, color = connection)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "CU-SeeMe frame rates", caption = "Simulated data", x = NULL, y = "Frames per second") +
  theme_cuseeme(base_size = 13)
```

## CueCat

`theme_cuecat()` uses the :CueCat barcode scanner: a pale paper background, a putty frame, a red title, red, ink, LED orange, and putty marks, and a Marker Felt title. Below we simulate weekly barcode scans after the free scanners shipped in 2000.

![Image: Shaddack, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:CueCat-upside.jpg), public domain.](../man/figures/theme_cuecat/cuecat-upside.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: cuecat
set.seed(2000)
scans <- data.frame(week = 1:52)
scans$scans <- rpois(52, 5000 * exp(-scans$week / 10))
ggplot(scans, aes(x = week, y = scans)) +
  geom_area(alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "CueCat scans", caption = "Simulated data", x = "Week", y = "Barcodes scanned") +
  theme_cuecat(base_size = 13)
```

## Doom

`theme_doom()`: hellfire red and orange on scorched brown. Below we simulate Doom frame rates by processor speed.

![Image: Bethesda, Copyright Microsoft, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Doom_classic_box_art.png), CC BY 3.0.](../man/figures/theme_doom/doom-classic-box-art.png){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: doom
set.seed(1993)
pcs <- data.frame(mhz = runif(100, 25, 100))
pcs$fps <- pmin(35, 0.45 * pcs$mhz + rnorm(100, 0, 3))
ggplot(pcs, aes(x = mhz, y = fps)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Doom frame rates", caption = "Simulated data", x = "CPU (MHz)", y = "Frames per second") +
  theme_doom(base_size = 13)
```

With `mode = "light"`:

```{r}
#| label: doom-light
last_plot() + theme_doom(base_size = 13, mode = "light")
```

## Fresh Prince

`theme_freshprince()` uses the logo: graffiti greens on a pink glow, and its continuous fill runs from teal to lime. Below we simulate how often the Carlton dance shows up each season.

![Image: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Fresh_Prince_Bel_Aire_logo.png), public domain.](../man/figures/theme_freshprince/fresh-prince-bel-aire-logo.png){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: freshprince
set.seed(1990)
fp <- expand.grid(season = 1:6, gag = c("Will flirts", "Carlton dance"))
fp$occurrences <- rbinom(12, 24, ifelse(fp$gag == "Will flirts", 0.9, plogis(-2.2 + 0.5 * (fp$season - 3.5))))
ggplot(fp, aes(x = season, y = gag, fill = occurrences)) +
  geom_tile() +
  labs(title = "Fresh Prince (simulated)", x = "Season", y = NULL, fill = "Episodes") +
  theme_freshprince(base_size = 13)
```

## Fruit Gushers

`theme_gushers()` uses a pile of Fruit Gushers on a white plate: a red frame and title, red, green, teal, orange, and pink marks, and a Chalkboard title. Below we simulate fruit snack trades at one lunch table before and after Gushers arrived in 1991.

![Image: Thomson200, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Betty_Crocker_Fruit_Gushers_pieces.jpg), CC0.](../man/figures/theme_gushers/betty-crocker-fruit-gushers-pieces.jpg){width="50%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: gushers
set.seed(1993)
trades <- expand.grid(year = 1985:2000, flavor = c("Strawberry", "Lime", "Blue raspberry"))
trades$n <- rpois(nrow(trades), ifelse(trades$year < 1991, 0.5, 3))
ggplot(subset(trades, n > 0), aes(x = year, y = flavor, color = flavor, alpha = n)) +
  geom_point(shape = 124, size = 6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Fruit Gushers", caption = "Simulated data", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_gushers(base_size = 13)
```

## Game Boy

`theme_gameboy()` uses the four shades of green from the original Game Boy screen and the pixel font Press Start 2P, which ships with `fmggp2`. Below we simulate the starter chosen by 300 *Pokémon Red and Blue* players.

![Image: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Game-Boy-FL.jpg), public domain.](../man/figures/theme_gameboy/game-boy-fl.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: gameboy
set.seed(1998)
pokemon_starters <- data.frame(
  starter = sample(c("Bulbasaur", "Charmander", "Squirtle"),
    size = 300, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.30, 0.42, 0.28))
)
ggplot(pokemon_starters, aes(x = starter, fill = starter)) +
  geom_bar(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Pokemon Red and Blue (simulated)",
       subtitle = "Starter chosen by 300 players",
       x = "Starter", y = "Count") +
  theme_gameboy(base_size = 13)
```

## GeoCities

`theme_geocities()`: lime text and a yellow Comic Sans title on a dark navy panel. Below we simulate GeoCities page loads.

![Image: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:GeoCities_logo.svg), public domain.](../man/figures/theme_geocities/geocities-logo.png){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: geocities
set.seed(1997)
pages <- data.frame(kb = rlnorm(2000, log(60), 0.45))
pages$seconds <- 2 + pages$kb * 8 / 44 + rnorm(2000, 0, 1.5)
ggplot(pages, aes(x = kb, y = seconds)) +
  geom_bin2d(bins = 25) +
  labs(title = "GeoCities page loads", caption = "Simulated data", x = "Page size (KB)", y = "Seconds to load") +
  theme_geocities(base_size = 13)
```

With `mode = "light"`:

```{r}
#| label: geocities-light
last_plot() + theme_geocities(base_size = 13, mode = "light")
```

## Goosebumps

`theme_goosebumps()`: the slime green logo and purple covers of the Goosebumps books on black, with a Trattatello title. Below we simulate Goosebumps books read by two grades.

```{r}
#| label: goosebumps
set.seed(1992)
readers <- data.frame(grade = rep(c("3rd grade", "5th grade"), each = 40))
readers$books <- rpois(80, ifelse(readers$grade == "3rd grade", 3, 9))
ggplot(readers, aes(x = books, fill = grade)) +
  geom_dotplot(method = "histodot", binwidth = 1, stackgroups = TRUE, binpositions = "all") +
  labs(title = "Goosebumps (simulated)", x = "Books read", fill = "Grade") +
  theme_goosebumps(base_size = 13)
```

With `mode = "light"`:

```{r}
#| label: goosebumps-light
last_plot() + theme_goosebumps(base_size = 13, mode = "light")
```

## Handspring Visor

`theme_visor()` uses a green Handspring Visor Deluxe: a pale lavender background, a translucent green frame, a gray LCD panel, green, gray, mint, and silver marks, and a Trebuchet MS title. Below we simulate sales of four Springboard modules.

![Image: Waldohreule, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Handspring_Visor_DeLuxe_Green.jpg), CC BY-SA 3.0.](../man/figures/theme_visor/handspring-visor-deluxe-green.jpg){width="40%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: visor
set.seed(2000)
modules <- data.frame(module = sample(c("Games", "MP3 player", "Modem", "Phone"),
  size = 500, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.35, 0.25, 0.25, 0.15)))
ggplot(modules, aes(y = module, fill = module)) +
  geom_bar(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Springboard modules", caption = "Simulated data", x = "Modules sold", y = NULL) +
  theme_visor(base_size = 13)
```

## Happy Meals

`theme_happymeal()` uses the red and yellow of a Happy Meal box. Below we simulate average daily Happy Meal sales for four toy promotions.

![Image: Newtown grafitti from Sydney, Australia, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Happy_meal_(6955434713).jpg), CC BY 2.0.](../man/figures/theme_happymeal/happy-meal-6955434713.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: happymeal
set.seed(1997)
happy_meals <- data.frame(promotion = c("Teenie Beanie Babies", "Furby", "Hot Wheels", "Inspector Gadget"),
  avg_sold = sapply(c(420, 310, 220, 180), function(l) mean(rpois(28, l))))
ggplot(happy_meals, aes(x = promotion, y = avg_sold, fill = promotion)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Happy Meals (simulated)", x = "Toy promotion", y = "Average sold per day") +
  theme_happymeal(base_size = 13)
```

## Hypercolor

`theme_hypercolor()`: heat changing magenta, orange, purple, and blue. Below we simulate monthly sales for two fads.

![Image: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Generra_Hypercolor_2.jpg), public domain.](../man/figures/theme_hypercolor/generra-hypercolor-2.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: hypercolor
months <- seq(1990, 1995, by = 1 / 12)
fads <- data.frame(month = rep(months, 2),
                   fad = rep(c("Hypercolor", "Slap bracelets"), each = length(months)))
fads$sales <- ifelse(fads$fad == "Hypercolor",
                     4000 * dnorm(fads$month, 1991.5, 0.6),
                     3000 * dnorm(fads$month, 1990.8, 0.4)) / 12
ggplot(fads, aes(x = month, y = sales, fill = fad)) +
  geom_area(alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "90s fads (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Sales (thousands)", fill = NULL) +
  theme_hypercolor(base_size = 13)
```

With `mode = "light"`:

```{r}
#| label: hypercolor-light
last_plot() + theme_hypercolor(base_size = 13, mode = "light")
```

## IBM Microdrive

`theme_microdrive()` uses an IBM and a Hitachi Microdrive on a tan desk: a black frame, a red title, IBM blue, red, navy, and Hitachi sky blue marks, and a Times New Roman title. Below we simulate photo file sizes from three digital cameras that wrote to a Microdrive.

![Image: MiNe, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:IBM_340MB_Microdrive_and_Hitachi_1GB_Microdrive_sold_from_Weikeng_Industrial_20080327.jpg), CC BY 2.0.](../man/figures/theme_microdrive/ibm-340mb-microdrive.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: microdrive
set.seed(1999)
photos <- data.frame(camera = rep(c("2 MP", "3 MP", "4 MP"), each = 100))
photos$mb <- rlnorm(300, log(c("2 MP" = 0.9, "3 MP" = 1.4, "4 MP" = 2)[photos$camera]), 0.25)
ggplot(photos, aes(x = camera, y = mb, fill = camera)) +
  geom_boxplot(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Microdrive photos", caption = "Simulated data", x = NULL, y = "Photo size (MB)") +
  theme_microdrive(base_size = 13)
```

## J2ME

`theme_j2me()` uses a Nokia N73 running a J2ME app: a black phone background, a silver frame, a pale screen panel, Ushahidi red, tan, brown, and black marks, and an Arial Narrow title. Below we simulate monthly downloads of four kinds of phone games.

![Image: Erik (HASH) Hersman, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ushahidi_J2ME_App.jpg), CC BY 2.0.](../man/figures/theme_j2me/ushahidi-j2me-app.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: j2me
set.seed(2003)
games <- expand.grid(month = 1:24, genre = c("Puzzle", "Racing", "Sports", "Arcade"))
games$downloads <- rpois(nrow(games), c(Puzzle = 60, Racing = 40, Sports = 30, Arcade = 20)[games$genre] * (1 + games$month / 12))
ggplot(games, aes(x = month, y = downloads, color = genre)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "J2ME game downloads", caption = "Simulated data", x = "Month", y = "Downloads (thousands)", color = NULL) +
  theme_j2me(base_size = 13)
```

## Java applets

`theme_javaapplet()` uses a Java AWT applet window: a gray window background, a gray frame, a white panel, red, blue, purple, and gray marks, and a blue Verdana title. Like the applet in the screenshot, below we simulate measurements with error bars and a fitted curve.

![Image: Audrius Meskauskas, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Java_applet.png), public domain.](../man/figures/theme_javaapplet/java-applet.png){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: javaapplet
set.seed(1995)
model <- data.frame(time = seq(0, 6, by = 0.1))
model$angle <- 48 * (1 - exp(-model$time / 1.2))
obs <- data.frame(time = seq(0, 6, by = 0.8))
obs$angle <- 48 * (1 - exp(-obs$time / 1.2)) + rnorm(nrow(obs), 0, 4)
ggplot(obs, aes(x = time, y = angle)) +
  geom_line(data = model, aes(color = "Model")) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = angle - 6, ymax = angle + 6, color = "Observed")) +
  labs(title = "Root bending angle", caption = "Simulated data", x = "Time (h)", y = "Angle (degrees)", color = NULL) +
  theme_javaapplet(base_size = 13)
```

## Jurassic Park

`theme_jurassic()` uses the Jurassic Park Post Office souvenir sheet: black, logo red, stamp yellow, and sunset orange. Below we simulate the total weight of the dinosaurs in each paddock.

```{r}

jp_paddocks <- data.frame(species = c("Brachiosaurus", "Triceratops", "Tyrannosaurus"),
  total_tons = c(sum(rnorm(3, 40, 5)), sum(rnorm(5, 9, 1.2)), sum(rnorm(2, 8, 1))))
ggplot(jp_paddocks, aes(x = species, y = total_tons, fill = species)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Jurassic Park (simulated)", x = "Paddock", y = "Total weight (tons)") +
  theme_jurassic(base_size = 13)
```

With `mode = "light"`:

```{r}
#| label: jurassic-light
last_plot() + theme_jurassic(base_size = 13, mode = "light")
```

## Novell NetWare

`theme_netware()` uses three NetWare 2.0 boxes: a pale blush background with dark ink text, a NetWare red frame and title, maroon, red, rose, and blush marks, and a Gill Sans title. Below we simulate the file servers running each NetWare version from 1990 to 1998.

## Y2K

`theme_y2k()`: LED red, terminal amber and green on black. Below we show how 300 households prepared for Y2K across three surveys.

![Image: Bug de l'an 2000, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bug_de_l%27an_2000.jpg), CC BY-SA 3.0.](../man/figures/theme_y2k/bug-de-l-an-2000.jpg){width="60%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: y2k
prep <- data.frame(
  survey = factor(rep(c("Jan", "Jul", "Dec"), each = 3), levels = c("Jan", "Jul", "Dec")),
  level = factor(rep(c("Not worried", "Some supplies", "Bunker ready"), 3),
                 levels = c("Not worried", "Some supplies", "Bunker ready")),
  households = c(163, 100, 37, 124, 119, 57, 108, 117, 75))
ggplot(prep, aes(x = survey, y = households, fill = level)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(title = "Y2K prep (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Households", fill = NULL) +
  theme_y2k(base_size = 13)
```

With `mode = "light"`:

```{r}
#| label: y2k-light
last_plot() + theme_y2k(base_size = 13, mode = "light")
```

## Fonts

`theme_gameboy()` and `theme_tetris()` use Press Start 2P, which ships with `fmggp2`. The other themes use fonts that ship with macOS and Windows.

These themes use Arial for the body text and a display font for the title:

- Impact (`theme_blockbuster()`)
- Arial Black (`theme_n64()` and `theme_freshprince()`)
- Herculanum (`theme_jurassic()`)
- Arial Rounded (`theme_happymeal()`)
- Bradley Hand (`theme_pogs()`)
- DIN Condensed (`theme_walkman()`)
- Courier New (`theme_oksoda()`)
- Brush Script (`theme_talkboy()`)
- Helvetica Neue (`theme_wired()`)
- Marker Felt (`theme_orbitz()`)
- Times New Roman (`theme_netscape()`)
- Big Caslon (`theme_titanic()`)
- Arial Rounded (`theme_koosh()`)
- Futura (`theme_tamagotchi()`)
- Arial Black (`theme_supersoaker()`)
- Trattatello (`theme_goosebumps()`)
- Skia (`theme_squeezit()`)
- Andale Mono (`theme_oregontrail()`)
- Arial Rounded (`theme_aim()`)
- Arial Narrow (`theme_rzone()`)
- DIN Condensed (`theme_batman()`)
- Arial Black (`theme_snick()`)
- SignPainter (`theme_savedbythebell()`)
- Gill Sans (`theme_hypercolor()`)
- PT Mono (`theme_y2k()`)
- Chalkboard (`theme_gushers()`)
- Impact (`theme_doom()`)
- Krungthep (`theme_consolewars()`)
- American Typewriter (`theme_seinfeld()`)
- Copperplate (`theme_powerrangers()`)
- Rockwell (`theme_bopit()`)
- Comic Sans MS (`theme_geocities()`)
- DIN Alternate (`theme_surge()`)
- Times New Roman (`theme_microdrive()`)
- Gill Sans (`theme_netware()`)
- Arial Narrow (`theme_j2me()`)
- Futura (`theme_palmpilot()`)
- Trebuchet MS (`theme_visor()`)
- Arial Black (`theme_pager()`)
- Tahoma (`theme_cuseeme()`)
- Andale Mono (`theme_vrml()`)
- Verdana (`theme_javaapplet()`)
- Marker Felt (`theme_cuecat()`)
- Arial Rounded (`theme_audrey()`)

When a font file can't be found, the theme falls back to `"sans"`, so the plots above still render on Linux. You can also pass any family you've registered with `sysfonts::font_add()`:

```{r}
#| label: family
#| eval: false
theme_oksoda(base_family = "sans", title_family = "sans")
```

## Using a theme for a whole chapter

Each chapter sets its theme once in the setup chunk with `theme_set()`, so the plotting code in the chapter doesn't need a `theme_*()` call.

```{r}
#| label: theme-set
#| eval: false
ggplot2::theme_set(fmggp2::theme_oksoda(base_size = 15))
```

The same works for the light version of a dark theme:

```{r}
#| label: theme-set-light
#| eval: false
ggplot2::theme_set(fmggp2::theme_doom(base_size = 15, mode = "light"))
```
